A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research on calibration and early-exit failure prediction, despite a changed title and substantial expansion. All pages, figures, tables, equations and appendices were readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original MSDNet experiments on CIFAR-100 and Tiny ImageNet, including temperature and rank-preserving decalibration, alternative calibration methods, and EEF1 evaluation.

after.justification: v3 reports original confidence-correction experiments across several architectures and datasets, with ablations, calibration comparisons, computational-cost measurements and distribution-shift evaluations.

M1.justification: v1 primarily proposes EEFP as an evaluation metric using existing classifier confidences. v3 Section 4.2 adds learned per-exit confidence correctors: MLPs trained with binary cross-entropy on EEFP stopping targets, using top-k probabilities and optionally previous exits' predictions. Their outputs replace classifier confidence for exit decisions.

E1.justification: CIFAR-100 and Tiny ImageNet remain covered. v3 adds ImageNet-1k and DomainNet, including training on real images and evaluation on five different domains: clipart, infograph, painting, quickdraw and sketch. This substantially extends both dataset coverage and input-distribution conditions.

E2.justification: v3 adds evaluated vector-scaling, matrix-scaling and architecture-matched confidence-target correction (CCCT) comparators in Table 9. Table 11 compares corrected, calibrated and uncorrected Gradient Equilibrium, Zero Time Waste and early-exit distillation systems. v1's LAP and LAP+MIE calibration comparisons are removed.

E3.justification: v3 adds ResNet, ViT and EfficientNet experimental configurations, pretrained ImageNet models, and controls that fit calibration and correction on the same held-out data, including matched-capacity CCCT comparisons. The budget-specific EEF1 evaluation is removed. The validation-based, exit-share threshold-selection procedure is retained.

E4.justification: v3 adds top-k sensitivity, prediction-history ablation, matched-architecture target comparisons, computational-overhead analysis, DomainNet robustness tests and transfer across early-exit systems. Temperature decalibration remains as a CIFAR-100 case study, while v1's rank-preserving decalibration, LAP/LAP+MIE sensitivity experiments and alternative EEF1 analysis are removed.

E5.justification: v1 reports averaging three independently initialized networks and displays shaded bands/error bars. v3 explicitly describes three calibrator/corrector initializations and tabulates standard deviations, while its main plots omit uncertainty displays. Three independently trained backbones are no longer specified; the PDFs do not establish an increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive numerical results for new methods and configurations. For example, Table 3 reports 64.06% accuracy for history-based correction versus 62.98% for calibration at the 50% FLOPs budget on ResNet-34/Tiny ImageNet. Results include counterexamples to uniform gains: Table 10 reports 10.51% versus 11.00% on Infograph at that budget. Several v1 analyses and their results disappear.

T1.justification: v3 introduces formal calibration definitions, EENN triviality and excess-risk analysis, a partition-refinement theorem, log-loss versus 0-1-loss results, and a stopping-probability proposition with an appendix proof. v1's temperature-scaling derivation and numerical counterexample survive in Appendix B; its monotonic-decalibration and EEF1 mathematics are removed.

C1.justification: v1's central contribution is that calibration can misrepresent early-exit performance and EEFP is a better proxy. v3 retains that claim but adds two central contributions: theoretical insufficiency of per-exit calibration without appropriate inter-exit structure, and a learned confidence-correction procedure claimed to improve cost-accuracy trade-offs across benchmarks.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations involving partition refinement, top-k regularization and prediction history, plus limitations concerning future-exit ordering, abstract grouping functions and transfer to cascades. v1's budget-specific EEFP caveat disappears. The new robustness interpretation also contains an error: Appendix F says calibration decreases unseen-domain ECE, whereas Table 10 shows increases in all five unseen domains.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-repository link, corrector architecture and training details, a 1000-epoch ceiling, early stopping and explicit absence of augmentation during calibration/correction. However, it omits v1's batch size 512, learning rate 0.001, zero weight decay, 2.5% calibration split and seven-block MSDNet specification. These are documentation changes, not evidence those settings changed.

R1.justification: v3 adds a dedicated related-work section positioning the work against model cascades, gating, monotonicity and risk-control approaches, alongside new calibration, anytime-computation and learning-to-defer foundations. It removes several earlier references, including Zhu et al. on calibration for failure prediction and Kristiadi et al. on Laplace approximation.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and background are extensively rewritten. The narrative changes from empirical counterexamples followed by a metric to a theory-method-experiments structure, with explicit contributions, related work, limitations and author contributions. Retained temperature-scaling and experimental-setup material is reorganized across the main text and appendices.

P2.justification: v3 changes the main text to two columns, adds a conceptual diagram and new benchmark plots, and introduces nine empirical tables. The original toy-example tables become Tables 5-6. The decalibration figure is reduced to CIFAR-100 and redrawn, while the rank-preserving, LAP/MIE and EEF1 figures are removed.

improvement.justification: v3's learned corrector, matched-capacity controls and broader evaluations substantially strengthen practical and empirical support. However, its new theory has unresolved problems: Proposition 3.3's within-group permutation conflicts with Definition 2.1's fixed group probabilities, and Section 4.1/Appendix A factor joint failures without establishing independence. The reversed ECE interpretation in Appendix F and omitted training settings further weaken reliability. These substantial benefits and reliability losses prevent a confident net-quality judgment.
